sentences.text: One party won almost two-thirds of the seats with a third of the votes. How?
Who can vote? From 18: British, Irish and Commonwealth citizens in the UK, plus Britons abroad.
The UK has 650 areas. In each, you put one cross next to one candidate.
Whoever gets the most votes wins the seat. Votes for everyone else win nothing.
The winners form the House of Commons, which makes laws and checks the government.
Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own parliaments for things like schools. England doesn't.
The House of Lords also checks laws, but isn't elected and can only delay them.
In 2024, Labour won 411 seats, so its leader became Prime Minister: first Keir Starmer, now Andy Burnham.
And the head of state? King Charles inherited the crown. He approves every law, but stays out of politics.
Is it fair that a third of the votes can win almost two-thirds of the seats?
